items.title: Section: Why "Pervasive," and Elder Revata's Question

items.zh: 如是四種所緣境事，遍行一切，隨入一切所緣境中，去來今世正等覺者共所宣說。是故說名遍滿所緣。又此所緣，遍毘鉢舍那品、遍奢摩他品、遍一切事、遍真實事、遍因果相屬事，故名遍滿。謂若說有分別影像，即是此中毘鉢舍那品。若說無分別影像，即是此中奢摩他品。若說事邊際性，即是此中一切事、真實事。若說所作成辦，即是此中因果相屬事。如佛世尊曾為長老頡隸伐多說如是義。曾聞長老頡隸伐多問世尊言：大德！諸有比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，能於所緣安住其心。為何於緣安住其心？云何於緣安住其心？齊何名為心善安住？佛告長老頡隸伐多：善哉！善哉！汝今善能問如是義。汝今諦聽，極善思惟，吾當為汝宣說開示。頡隸伐多！諸有比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，能於所緣安住其心。或樂淨行、或樂善巧、或樂令心解脫諸漏，於相稱緣安住其心，於相似緣安住其心，於緣無倒安住其心，能於其中不捨靜慮。
items.en: These four objects of meditation pervade every practice, entering into every object of meditation whatsoever, taught alike by the fully awakened ones of the past, future, and present — for this reason they are called pervasive objects. … It is heard that the elder Revata once asked the Blessed One: Venerable one, monks who diligently cultivate meditative practice, such yoga masters, are able to settle the mind on their object. Why do they settle the mind on the object? How do they settle the mind on the object? To what degree is the mind said to be genuinely well settled? … Revata! Monks who diligently cultivate meditative practice, such yoga masters, settle the mind on their object — whether delighting in purifying practice, in skilful understanding, or in freeing the mind from every outflow — by settling the mind on a matched object, settling it on a corresponding object, settling it on an undistorted object, and, throughout, never abandoning meditative absorption.

items.zh: 云何比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於相稱緣安住其心？謂彼比丘若唯有貪行，應於不淨緣安住於心，如是名為於相稱緣安住其心。若唯有瞋行，應於慈愍安住其心；若唯有癡行，應於緣性緣起安住其心；若唯有慢行，應於界差別安住其心；若唯有尋思行，應於阿那波那念安住其心。如是名為於相稱緣安住其心。頡隸伐多！又彼比丘若愚諸行自相，愚我、有情、命者、生者、能養育者、補特伽羅事，應於蘊善巧安住其心。若愚其因，應於界善巧安住其心。

items.title: Section: Revata's Dialogue Closes — Four Purities From Sustained Practice

items.zh: 若愚其緣，應於處善巧安住其心。若愚無常、苦、空、無我，應於緣起、處非處善巧安住其心。若樂離欲界欲，應於諸欲麁性、諸色靜性安住其心；若樂離色界欲，應於諸色麁性、無色靜性安住其心。若樂通達及樂解脫遍一切處薩迦耶事，應於苦諦、集諦、滅諦、道諦安住其心。是名比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於相稱緣安住其心。頡隸伐多！云何比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於相似緣安住其心？謂彼比丘，於彼彼所知事，為欲簡擇、極簡擇、遍尋思、遍伺察故，於先所見、所聞、所覺、所知事，由見聞覺知增上力故，以三摩呬多地作意，思惟分別而起勝解。彼雖於其本所知事不能和合現前觀察，然與本事相似而生，於彼所緣有彼相似唯智、唯見、唯正憶念。又彼比丘，於時時間令心寂靜，於時時間依增上慧法毘鉢舍那勤修觀行。是名比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於相似緣安住其心。頡隸伐多！云何比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於緣無倒安住其心？謂若比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於所緣境安住其心，隨應解了所知境界，如實無倒能遍了知。是名比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，於緣無倒安住其心。頡隸伐多！云何比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，能於其中不捨靜慮？謂若比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，如是於緣正修行時，無間加行、殷重加行，於時時間修習止相、舉相、捨相。由修、由習、由多修習為因緣故，一切麁重悉皆息滅，隨得觸證所依清淨。於所知事，由現見故，隨得觸證所緣清淨。由離貪故，隨得觸證心遍清淨。離無明故，隨得觸證智遍清淨。
items.en: For confusion about conditions, one should settle the mind on sense-field skillfulness. For confusion about impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, one should settle the mind on dependent-origination skillfulness and possible-and-impossible skillfulness. To wish detachment from the desire realm, one should settle the mind on the coarseness of desire and the calm of form; to wish detachment from the form realm, on the coarseness of form and the calm of the formless. To wish direct realisation and liberation from self-view pervading every realm, one should settle the mind on the truths of suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. … A monk who diligently cultivates meditative practice settles the mind on the object, understanding what should be known correctly and thoroughly, without distortion. … Such a monk, rightly practising on the object this way, applies unbroken and earnest effort, cultivating, from time to time, the marks of calming, of uplifting, and of equanimity. Through cultivating, repeating, and extensively practising this, all coarse residue is extinguished, and one attains, in turn, purity of basis. Through directly seeing the known matter, one attains purity of object. Through freedom from craving, one attains purity pervading the mind. Through freedom from ignorance, one attains purity pervading wisdom.

items.zh: 是名比丘勤修觀行，是瑜伽師，能於其中不捨靜慮。

blocks.text: The treatise grounds the four objects in a sūtra: the Buddha's answer to the monk Revata. One short passage (0428a10) is untranslated.

"These four objects pervade every practice, taught alike by the fully awakened ones of the past, future, and present." Master Cháng Bǎi: even the mundane path that attains a root absorption has a kind of direct knowledge, but only the supramundane completes the task.
Revata asks: how should a monk who practises yoga settle the mind on an object? Venerable Miào Jìng: his name means "meeting the time"; Master Cháng Bǎi: born when the Buddha appeared.

The Buddha: settle the mind "on a matched object, on a corresponding object, on an undistorted object". If the monk is of desire-type, on impurity; anger-type, loving-kindness; delusion-type, dependent origination; pride-type, analysis of the elements; discursive-type, mindfulness of breathing.

"For confusion about the self-nature of phenomena, settle the mind on the aggregates; for confusion about causes, on the elements; for confusion about conditions, on the sense-fields; for confusion about impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, on dependent origination." And for freedom from desire, on the coarse and calm of each level, or on the four truths.
"Through freedom from craving, one attains purity pervading the mind; through freedom from ignorance, purity pervading wisdom." With sustained practice, one reaches four purities.

quiz.q: The English renders 無分別現量智見 as "undefiled direct realisation." What different view does Master Cháng Bǎi relay from the commentary?
options: even the mundane path, attaining root absorption, has non-discriminating direct knowledge, though with an image — still mundane; "undefiled" is added by the English
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mundane path attains a root absorption, non-discriminating direct knowledge also arises — yet with an image, seemingly real, still classed as mundane. He himself judges it the undefiled absorptions of the non-learner, admitting the text does not say so; "undefiled" is not in the original.

quiz.q: The questioner 頡隸伐多 is rendered "the elder Kṣitigarbha." What do the lectures say?
options: 頡隸伐多 means "meeting the time," a monk of the Buddha's day (Revata), not Kṣitigarbha
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 頡隸伐多 translates as "meeting the time." Master Cháng Bǎi: he was born when the Buddha appeared in the world. The English mistakes the name for Kṣitigarbha throughout §33–35.

quiz.q: What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for a "matched" object?
options: a doctor's prescription that matches the illness
quiz.why: "Settling the mind on a matched object, settling it on a corresponding object, settling it on an undistorted object." Venerable Miào Jìng: when a doctor treats us, the medicine prescribed fits our illness — that too is "matched."

quiz.q: Through sustained practice one attains four purities. What comes through freedom from craving, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say of their order?
options: purity pervading the mind; basis and object first, then mind and wisdom — the order can be reversed
quiz.why: "Through freedom from craving, one attains purity pervading the mind. Through freedom from ignorance, one attains purity pervading wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: the text gives purity of basis and of object first, then of mind and wisdom — it could also be stated the other way round.
